title: a native pin whose graph reaches a host module through a project module's named re-export fails to compile, and the diagnostic names the laundering module
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin', is the rule: the assertion is over the COMPLETE TRANSITIVE GRAPH, so a requirement reached one module away is the same requirement. `Module<"node:fs">` is poc/src/targets/classify.ts's concrete spelling of the JavaScript-host dependence the same page names, and `blocksNativePin` refuses `TypeScript`, `Module<...>` and `Host<...>` together. This is the laundered half of 21-native-pin/a-pin-reaching-a-host-module-is-rejected: the two cases are the same program apart from the specifier on line 2, so a pin rule that answers them differently is answering the specifier rather than the graph. The SMITHERS1510 companion lands in the .mod.sm file, at the re-export, because a re-export runs the target module's initializer exactly as an import does; it is declared rather than filtered because a cascade the language really does produce is part of the contract (conformance/README.md). `messageContains` pins the second half of the rule — the SHOULD sentence about the dependency path — because a pin refused with an empty route would satisfy a code-and-position expectation exactly and leave the route unpinned. Before this case existed, zero of the corpus's .sm files contained a re-export in any area, so this whole surface was uncontracted. RETIRED MARKER (go, 2026-08-23): the fork used to accept this program, grant the pin and print `9` — zero diagnostics where the reference reports SMITHERS1510@4:30 in reexport-host-module.mod.sm and SMITHERS3001@17:1 in the case — because its dependency walk stopped at the first import declaration and never asked what the target module re-exports. The fork now walks export declarations and follows a referenced value to its real runtime edge (`nativeLaunderWalk`, compiler/forkbridge/nativepin.go.txt), and it satisfies this case's declared route `-> reexport-host-module.mod.sm -> node:fs` rather than merely producing the code; measured XPASS on go by `node conformance/runner/run.mjs --backend both --jobs 4`.
